title: Submerged page
blurb: A live interactive HTML form drawn beneath a real-time 2D shallow-water heightfield in one WebGL 2 canvas. The fragment shader bends the DOM with Snell refraction, draws Jacobian optical caustics across the text and keeps a movable shoreline meniscus while buttons, sliders and touch scroll stay usable.
question: Can a live interactive HTML form stay legible and clickable beneath a real-time 2D wave-equation water surface with Snell refraction, optical caustics, and an interactive shoreline meniscus, without per-frame CPU readback or losing touch scroll?
result: Not verified yet in a live browser. One ElementGL canvas uploads the live HTML form via texElementSubImage2D(), steps a 128 by 128 shallow-water PDE heightfield on the CPU into an RGBA8 height-and-gradient texture, renders Snell refraction with Jacobian caustics and a movable shoreline meniscus, and syncs hit boxes with updateElementGeometry().
